newsitem.title: CHINA: Hongkong Bank prints handover notes, lots of them.
newsitem.headline: Hongkong Bank prints handover notes, lots of them.

text.p: Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp is making a quick buck and a lot of them, literally.
Hongkong Bank, one of the territory's three note-issuing banks, said on Monday that it is introducing a special banknote to mark the establishment of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
The notes, to be circulated from Tuesday, will be dated July 1, 1997 to mark the day of Hong Kong's return to China after more than 150 years of British rule.
The new notes will have exactly the same design as those issued in 1993.

Aside from the special date and a reconfiguration of the serial number -- the first million of each denomination will carry the prefix AA -- the only other change will be the signature on the notes, which will be that of the bank's current general manager, Christopher Langley.
But bad news for collectors hoping to make a quick buck themselves -- Hongkong Bank said the new notes are being circulated with existing notes and "will be in plentiful supply".
